title: Indian independence
group: HIST-TOPIC — Overview Anchors (each links to deeper subdomains)
examples: What were the main goals of the early independence movements?
How did the Partition of India affect people's lives?
Can you explain the difference between non-violent and violent resistance?

explain.say: The first phase saw early calls for reform and limited self-rule.
The second phase involved mass movements demanding complete independence from Britain.
The third phase saw growing political demands and negotiations with the British government.
The partition of India was the painful division of the subcontinent into new nations.
In everyday life, understanding historical change helps us see how societies evolve.
A common mistake is forgetting that the struggle was long and involved many people.

faq.q: Why was the period after independence so difficult?
faq.a: The immediate aftermath involved managing massive population shifts and political disagreements. It was complex because of the division.
asks: What were the challenges right after 1947?
Was it easy to build the new nations?

faq.q: What did the Non-Cooperation Movement actually involve?
faq.a: It involved withdrawing cooperation from British institutions, like schools and courts. People boycotted government activities.
asks: How did people protest without violence?

faq.q: Who were the main leaders during the freedom struggle?
faq.a: Many leaders contributed, including Mahatma Gandhi, Jawaharlal Nehru, and Sardar Patel. Their efforts spanned decades.
asks: Who was most important in the movement?

faq.q: Why was the partition so emotionally charged?
faq.a: It was a sudden division based on religion, forcing millions of people to move and leading to violence. It separated communities.
asks: What was the main cause of the division?

faq.q: What was the difference between the two main phases?
faq.a: The early phases focused on asking for reforms, while the later phases demanded complete self-rule and independence.
asks: How did the goals change over time?
What marked the shift in demands?

facts: The Indian National Congress was a key political body in the struggle.
The Non-Cooperation Movement encouraged boycotts of foreign goods.
The partition led to massive migrations of people.
The Quit India Movement was a direct call for immediate British withdrawal.

quiz.say: The early phase of the movement focused on:

options.show: D. Focusing only on economic boycotts.
options.say: D. Focusing only on economic boycotts.

options.show: A. Seeking limited reforms and representation.
options.say: A. Seeking limited reforms and representation.

quiz.why: This is correct because the initial demands were for changes within the British system, not immediate separation.

wrong.0: This is tempting because the final goal was independence, but the early phase was more gradual.
wrong.1: This is wrong because the early movements emphasized non-violent methods of protest.
wrong.2: This is too narrow; the early phase involved political and social reform demands too.

quiz.say: The Civil Disobedience Movement was characterized by:

options.show: C. Only involving upper-class educated men.
options.say: C. Only involving upper-class educated men.

options.show: D. Being limited only to the cities.
options.say: D. Being limited only to the cities.

quiz.why: This describes civil disobedience, which is the peaceful refusal to obey certain laws.

wrong.0: The movement was fundamentally non-violent in its core methods.
wrong.1: The movement successfully mobilized the masses, including peasants and women.
wrong.2: The movement spread deeply into the rural areas across India.

quiz.say: The division of the subcontinent into India and Pakistan primarily resulted from:

options.show: D. Economic competition between the regions.
options.say: D. Economic competition between the regions.

options.show: A. Religious differences leading to separate homelands.
options.say: A. Religious differences leading to separate homelands.

options.show: B. A failure of the British to manage taxes.
options.say: B. A failure of the British to manage taxes.

options.show: C. A sudden military invasion by a third power.
options.say: C. A sudden military invasion by a third power.

quiz.why: The basis for the partition was the distinct religious identities of the major communities.

wrong.0: Economic factors were secondary to the deeply rooted religious and cultural identities.
wrong.2: While administration was involved, the primary driver was religious communalism.
wrong.3: The partition was a political agreement and consequence, not a military conquest.
